dataStrategy.title: FY2026-2030 Data Strategy
dataStrategy.summary: DHA frames data as a trusted, mission-enabling strategic asset across combat support, healthcare delivery, and operational efficiency. Five lines of effort define the operating model. Source-backed vendor implications below.

lines_of_effort.name: Data Roles and Responsibilities
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Governance, RACI documentation, data-steward enablement, training pipelines, role-based access design.

lines_of_effort.name: Authoritative Data Sources (ADS)
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: ADS designation services, source-of-truth analytics, deduplication, system-of-record consolidation.

lines_of_effort.name: Operationalizing Data as a Product
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Product-oriented data engineering, consumer-grade interfaces, SLAs, lifecycle ownership, internal data-product teams.

lines_of_effort.name: Data Quality and Transparency
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Enterprise data quality scorecards, automated lineage, observability tooling, public-facing quality dashboards.

lines_of_effort.name: Enterprise Data Catalog (EDC)
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Catalog metadata governance, ADS registration workflows, integration with EDC, search and discovery layers.

items.label: Ambient Listening
items.context: Limited fielding completed 2025; full DoD enterprise deployment began February 2026

contractorRead: DHA's data strategy is the dominant capture signal for FY2026-2030. Vendors with productized data-engineering offerings, ADS-readiness assessments, EDC-integration experience, or data-quality observability tooling get a directly relevant lane. On the EHR side, MHS GENESIS is in worldwide sustainment posture, which moves the work into change orders, sustainment integrators, and ambient-clinical-documentation buildout rather than a new core competition. Position around demonstrable lineage, source-of-truth governance, and product-team operating models, not generic analytics.

watchNext.signal: Ambient clinical documentation enterprise rollout (Feb 2026 start)
DHMSM sustainment task orders against deployment-integrator vehicles
Authoritative Data Source designation rollouts under the FY2026-2030 Data Strategy

name: Department of Health and Human Services
type: Cabinet Department (parent of CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, ARPA-H)
description: Department-level map. HHS itself sets policy and coordinates; the buying happens through its operating divisions. Map: CMS (Medicare, Medicaid, claims), NIH (research IT, NITAAC), FDA (Sentinel, regulated-product data), CDC (data modernization, DCIPHER), IHS (PATH EHR), ONC (interoperability, certification), ARPA-H (OTA-funded R&D).
mmtRead: HHS IT spend is decentralized. Treat HHS as a navigation layer: route procurement questions to the operating division that owns the program (CMS for claims, NIH for research IT, FDA for surveillance, etc.). The departmental level is for policy and rulemaking, not contract awards.
procurementSignals: See operating division profiles for actual procurement
openVehicles: See CMS / NIH / NITAAC for operating-division vehicles
current_read: HHS at the department level coordinates policy. Buying flows through CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, and ARPA-H. Use the operating-division profiles for actual procurement opportunities.
key_offices: Operating Divisions (CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, ARPA-H)

policyModule.title: HHS Enterprise AI and Digital Governance
confirmed_facts: HHS frames its AI work as making AI available to the federal workforce and integrating AI across internal operations, research, and public health.
The official AI strategy themes are: driving AI innovation, improving AI governance, and fostering public trust in federal AI use.
The current public-facing AI artifact does not specify contract clauses, purchasing vehicles, or procurement requirements.
vendor_watch: Governance artifacts: model documentation, evaluation frameworks, audit-ready logs, bias and fairness measurement.
Workforce enablement: AI literacy, role-specific training, secure model access for federal employees.
Responsible implementation: explainability, content provenance, safety/security review documentation.
Public-trust posture: transparency reports, plain-language disclosures, third-party assurance options.
Do not market HHS AI procurement requirements that the public page does not state. Treat as watch, not confirmed buy.

contractorRead: HHS is a regulator-of-self for AI rollout across operating divisions, not a single buyer. Treat HHS-level AI direction as setting tone for CMS, CDC, FDA, IHS, NIH operating-division procurements. The right capture move is to map each governance theme to the operating division that actually buys, then position there.

watchNext.signal: HHS AI compliance plan publications and operating-division alignment activity

sources.label: HHS AI Strategy & Implementation
sources.caveat: Page does not state contract clauses, vehicles, or procurement requirements. Vendor implications are watch items, not confirmed buys.

name: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
type: HHS Sub-Office (regulatory, not a primary buyer)
description: Sets health IT interoperability standards, certifies EHR technology under ONC Health IT Certification, owns USCDI evolution, runs TEFCA implementation through the RCE (Sequoia Project), and enforces information blocking under 45 CFR Part 171.
mmtRead: ONC's procurement footprint is small. Its regulatory leverage is enormous: USCDI determines what data EHRs must exchange, TEFCA determines who participates in the network, and information blocking enforcement determines who pays the penalty. Track ONC for what it enables, not what it buys.

at_risk: ONC budget is small and vulnerable to broader HHS cuts

current_read: ONC is enforcing TEFCA and expanding USCDI. Information blocking enforcement actions are increasing. ONC procurement is limited but its regulatory decisions shape billions in private-sector and government health IT spending.

policyModule.title: HTI-2 Final Rule + TEFCA
confirmed_facts: The HTI-2 final rule finalizes TEFCA-related provisions supporting electronic health information access, exchange, and use.
The rule establishes 45 CFR Part 172 for TEFCA-related provisions.
The rule amends information-blocking regulations by adding TEFCA Manner Exception definitions.
The rule makes no changes to the existing TEFCA Manner Exception at 45 CFR § 171.403.
vendor_watch: TEFCA transparency and reliability documentation as a deliverable compliance artifact set.
QHIN ecosystem positioning: partnership, integration, or QHIN-adjacent service models.
Information-blocking compliance posture as a product attribute, not only a legal review.
Privacy, security, and trust documentation built to TEFCA Manner Exception expectations.

contractorRead: ASTP/ONC is a standards regulator, not a conventional buyer. Vendor capture moves are around compliance positioning, certification-mark readiness, and QHIN-ecosystem integration. Treat ONC rule activity as a market-shaping signal that flows into every downstream HHS, VA, DOD, and commercial EHR procurement.

mmtRead: ARPA-H's procurement model is the access lever. OTA awards are not constrained by FAR-style competition rules, which is why non-traditional vendors and academic-industry teams can win. Watch ADVOCATE (agentic clinical AI), Sprint for Women's Health, and the next program announcement wave for FY2027.

2026 SBIR/STTR topics published; TIGAR Exploratory Topic open.

contractorRead: ARPA-H runs a programmatic, ISO-driven model. The Mission Office ISO lane is the perpetual front door: rolling, gated by Solution Summary feedback, and matched to four named offices. Capture posture is to pick the office, study its strategic direction, write a Solution Summary that maps to it, and use the feedback step as your iteration loop. Treat program ISOs as time-boxed RFP equivalents.

policyModule.title: CMS Health Technology Ecosystem
confirmed_facts: CMS describes the Health Technology Ecosystem as a collaborative vision to modernize the national digital health ecosystem, empower Medicare beneficiaries, improve outcomes, reduce provider burden, and drive value.
The official page highlights voluntary alignment of data networks, EHR systems, health app developers, providers, and innovators around a shared framework for data and access.

The page references expansion of CMS data-sharing capabilities, modern identity on Medicare.gov, launch of public infrastructure for provider data, and an RFI regarding digital health products for Medicare beneficiaries and interoperability infrastructure.
vendor_watch: Data-sharing expansion: identity-resolution, FHIR-mediated APIs, beneficiary-consent management.
Modern identity on Medicare.gov: identity proofing, multi-factor authentication, account-recovery flows, accessibility.
National Provider Directory: provider-data ingestion, validation, deduplication, dissemination services.
RFI engagement: position now on digital health products + interoperability infrastructure to influence framing.

contractorRead: CMS is positioning as an ecosystem-builder, not only a buyer. The voluntary-alignment framing matters: CMS is signaling influence comes from showing up to the framework, not waiting on an RFP. The Provider Directory and Medicare.gov identity work are concrete infrastructure builds with clear vendor surfaces. The RFI is the leading indicator of the FY2027-FY2028 buy.

watchNext.signal: National Provider Directory infrastructure build + Medicare.gov identity modernization steps
Digital-health-products RFI responses and downstream interoperability-infrastructure activity

mmtRead: IHS PATH is the active EHR modernization arc — replacing RPMS with Oracle Health on the GDIT platform. Tribal health IT procurement intersects with both federal contracting and tribal sovereignty considerations, which constrains what vendors can compete and how.
keyPrograms: PATH EHR Modernization (Oracle Health, GDIT prime, RPMS replacement)
current_read: PATH is the active modernization. Tribal sovereignty considerations shape competition.

name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
description: Federal public health agency. Buys data modernization, surveillance, and analytics tooling through DMI, PHDS, DIBBs, and DCIPHER (Palantir Foundry-based). State, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT) adoption of DIBBs tools is a tracked metric.
mmtRead: CDC's procurement focus is data modernization. DMI is the umbrella; PHDS is the data services layer; DIBBs is the toolkit; DCIPHER is the Palantir-based surveillance platform. The 2026 target is greater than 30 percent STLT adoption of at least one DIBBs product.
procurementSignals: DIBBs STLT adoption acceleration (2026 target greater than 30 percent)
current_read: CDC is driving DIBBs adoption at the STLT level and continuing DCIPHER expansion on Palantir Foundry.

name: Food and Drug Administration
description: Regulates food, drugs, biologics, devices, and tobacco. Buys post-market surveillance and regulated-product data systems through Sentinel, market-research vehicles, and operating-division IT modernization. Sentinel 3.0 market research is active (75F40126SSN00100).
mmtRead: FDA Sentinel is the flagship post-market drug surveillance program. Sentinel 3.0 is in market-research stage with eight tiers spanning data broker services (1-6), GOCO platform (Tier 7), and scientific support (Tier 8). NAICS 518210.
procurementSignals: Sentinel 3.0 sources sought 75F40126SSN00100 (closed Mar 23 2026; full RFP expected 2026)

name: National Institutes of Health / NIH IT Acquisition and Assessment Center
description: NIH is the country's biomedical research agency. NITAAC is NIH's acquisition center and runs CIO-SP3 / CIO-SP4 (canceled) / CIO-CS — the NIH GWACs that anchor IT procurement across HHS. Treat NIH as both a research buyer and an acquisition channel for the rest of HHS.
mmtRead: CIO-SP4 was canceled (SAM Amendment 0017 on RFP 75N98121R00001). CIO-SP3 is the active bridge through Apr 29 2027. CIO-CS is the IT commodities vehicle and a follow-on (`The Store`) is in pre-RFP at a reported $20B-$25B.
current_read: CIO-SP4 canceled. CIO-SP3 bridges through Apr 29 2027. CIO-CS follow-on in pre-RFP.

name: General Services Administration
description: Acquisition channel only. GSA runs Alliant 3 (active, no ceiling), Polaris (small business), 8(a) STARS III ($50B), and OASIS+ (governmentwide professional services). Track GSA vehicles for the access lane, not for the agency mission itself.
